text:
incident-bot: ALERT: service p99 spike detected on /v1/generate-stream (p99=1.45s, SLO=1.2s). Spike started ~15m ago. paging to #incidents :rotating_light:

maria gonzalez: folks, customer reports of truncated streams and long tails. Oncall, can you confirm scope?

eng-sre-oncall: pulling metrics now. p95 ~400ms, p99 ~1450ms from 2025-03-15T02:04 -> now. streaming_disconnect_rate increased from 0.9% -> 6.2%.

liam chen: I have a correlating signal: `prefix_cache_hit_rate` collapsed from ~86% to ~9% cluster-wide starting at ~02:03. KV put rate spiked as cold keys cause backend fills.

nina r: any infra deploys or config changes around 02:00?

eng-runtime: we rolled `prefix-salt` update under feature flag `prefix_hash_v2` at 01:58 to 30% of serving nodes to address rare collision cases. Release id `rwd-runtime-20250315-03`.

ajay singh: if the hash changed, cached keys will diverge. Did we include dual-key compatibility?

eng-runtime: no, we relied on a migration plan that assumed stateless keys. We overlooked overlap behavior.

liam chen: quick check across nodes shows mixed keyspace: nodes with v2 are producing different bucket prefixes. Example logs:```text
[02:05:12] node-77 GET prefix:v1:xyz -> MISS
[02:05:12] node-105 GET prefix:v2:xyz -> HIT
```

maria gonzalez: customers: 7 high-priority tickets opened in the last 20m, multiple report partial output. Need mitigation ASAP + customer comms.

eng-sre-oncall: mitigation options: (A) Flip flag off (revert to v1) across nodes (fast), (B) Patch serving code to try v1 then v2 (dual-lookup) (medium), (C) Full rollback release (slow). Which gives fastest low-risk recovery?

eng-runtime: flipping flag to disable `prefix_hash_v2` should restore prev behavior quickly. However, some nodes might have warmed new keys causing a brief transitional miss window. Dual-lookup would avoid rehydration but requires building and deploying a tiny patch; could be done as a hotfix in ~30-40m.

liam chen: given customer impact, let's flip the flag first and monitor. If rolling flip doesn't improve within 8 minutes, consider hotfix for dual-lookup.

ajay singh: executing feature flag rollback now. Command:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://config.internal/api/flags/prefix_hash_v2 -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"value":"off","note":"incident rollback"}'
```

eng-runtime: canary group (5% nodes) rolled to off at 1951006815. Observing metrics for canary nodes.

eng-sre-oncall: canary signals: prefix_cache_hit_rate on canary group climbed from 10% -> 78% within 90s. p99 on canary nodes dropped to ~680ms.

nina r: promising. If canary behaves, ramping should quickly restore cluster hit rates.

maria gonzalez: drafting comms: "We observed an internal config change affecting prefix hashing that temporarily reduced cache hit rates and caused streaming latency. We're rolling the change back and will update soon." Posting to #customer-comms after you confirm mitigation.

eng-runtime: ramping flag to 100% rollback at 1951006855.

liam chen: running a targeted cache warmup on the oldest shards to speed rehydration:```bash
./tools/warm_prefix_cache --shards shard-1,shard-3,shard-7 --sample 150k
``` Warmup kicked at 1951006862.

eng-sre-oncall: cluster metrics 3m after full rollback (1951007040): p95=360ms, p99=560ms, streaming_disconnect_rate down to 1.4%. Cluster prefix_cache_hit_rate recovered to ~83%.

support-bot: Customer notifications sent (IDs: COM-789, COM-790). Support tickets 4625,4626,4630 updated to "mitigated".

maria gonzalez: good. We'll need a post-incident follow-up. Immediate asks for postmortem: root cause, why migration plan didn't account for live cache, and a safe rollout plan.

liam chen: root cause draft: feature-flagged prefix-salt change created incompatible key format; partial rollout caused mixed keyspace and mass cold misses -> extra backend load -> increased tail latency and streaming stalls.

nina r: additional contributing factors: no pre-rollout parity check for cache hit-rate, canary size too small to reveal streaming-heavy shard behavior, no fallback dual-lookup in serving.

ajay singh: proposed short-term actions: 1) Enforce dual-lookup fallback during any hash migration for 72 hours; 2) Add a rollout gate that checks prefix_cache_hit_rate parity (delta >10% abort); 3) Increase canary to 15% for hash migrations to better sample shard diversity. I'll own 1 & 3.

eng-runtime: I'll own action 2 and add an automated parity check into the deployment pipeline. Target dates: dual-lookup patch by 48h, parity gate in CI by 72h, canary size policy doc by EOD tomorrow.

liam chen: I'll prepare an ops playbook for quick warmup and flag rollback steps and add an alert runbook for streaming-tail-stall_count >2x baseline.

maria gonzalez: customer comms follow-up: send a post-incident summary 3-4 hours after final verification. I'll coordinate language with support.

eng-sre-oncall: handing over to night oncall at 1951007180. Night oncall please monitor: p99, streaming_disconnect_rate, prefix_cache_hit_rate, and KV backend CPU.

nina r: log sample to include in postmortem:```json
{"time":"02:06:01","node":"node-105","prefix_key":"v2:abc","cache_hit":true}
{"time":"02:06:01","node":"node-77","prefix_key":"v1:abc","cache_hit":false}
```

maria gonzalez: adding that to the timeline. Anything else before we close the incident channel?

eng-runtime: let's keep this thread open for postmortem links. I'll attach PR links when ready.

maria gonzalez: thanks all, marking incident as mitigated. Will publish incident summary and link to postmortem once drafted. :white_check_mark:
